result.topic_en: Diary entries from September–October 1796 on the inversion of the integral of dx/sqrt(1-x^n) (lemniscatic-type functions), a method for transforming equations, rationalising denominators of fractions with irrational quantities, auxiliary equations for elimination, a new approach to the general solution of equations, the roots of x^n-1, and the cubic equation for the cubic periods when n is prime.
result.transcription:
Si $\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-x^3)}}$ stat. $\Pi:x = z$ [?] $\&$ [?] $x=\Phi:z$ erit
$\Phi:z = z - \frac{1}{8}z^4 + \frac{1}{112}z^7 - \frac{1}{1792}z^{10} + \frac{3}{1792\cdot 52}z^{13} - \frac{3.185}{1792.52.14.15.16}z^{16}$ Sept. 9
Si $\Phi\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-x^n)}} = x$ erit:
$\Phi:z = z - \frac{1}{2.n+1}z^n A + \frac{n-1}{4.2n+1}z^n B - \frac{nn-n-1}{2.n+1.3n+1}C\ldots$
Methodus facilis inveniendi aeq: in y ex aeq. in x si ponatur $x^n + ax^{n-1} + bx^{n-2} \ldots = y$ Sept. 14
fractiones quarum denominator continet quantitates irrationales (quomodocunque?) in alias transmutare ab hoc incommodo liberatas. Sept. 16
Coefficientes aeq: auxiliariae eliminationi inservientis ex radicibus aeq: datae determinati eod.
Nova methodus qua resolutionem aequationum universalem investigare forsitanque invenire licebit Sept. 17.
Scil. transm: aeq: in aliam cuius radices
$\alpha\zeta' + \beta\zeta'' + \gamma\zeta''' + \ldots$ ubi $\sqrt[n]{1} = \alpha, \beta$ etc. $\&$ n numerum aequationis gradum denotans
In mentem mihi venit radices aeq. $x^n-1$ ex aeq., communes radices habentibus elicere ut adeo pleramque tantum aequationes coefficientibus rationalibus gaudent[-ibus-]es resolui oporteat Sept. 29 Bruns.
Aequatio tertii gradus est haec: $x^3 + xx - nx + \frac{nn-3n-1-mp}{3} = 0$ ubi $3n+1=p$ $\&$ m numerus resid. cubicorum similes sui excipientes. Unde sequitur si $n=3k$ fore $m+1=3l$ si $n=3k\pm1$ fore $m=3l$. Octob. 1 Bruns.
Sive $z^3 - 3pz + (pp-8p-9pm) = 0$
Hoc m penitus determinatum $m+1$ semper $\square + 3\square$

items.english: A new method by which it will be possible to investigate, and perhaps find, the universal solution of equations.

items.quote: Unde sequitur si $n=3k$ fore $m+1=3l$ si $n=3k\pm1$ fore $m=3l$.
items.english: From which it follows that if n=3k then m+1=3l, if n=3k±1 then m=3l.
This m is completely determined; m+1 is always a square plus three times a square.
